title: Invoice Enrollment Standard for Patient Payment Plans
content:
Patient Services applies this standard to every invoice put on a **Patient Payment Plans** plan, whether at the offer or later. Each test is read from the company's records — the invoice's own status, billing class and balance due, and the plan's status — never from the patient's description of them.

## Conditions on the invoice

1. **Open invoices only.** An invoice can be enrolled only while its own status is open. An invoice on hold, in collections, already on a plan, paid or closed cannot be enrolled.
2. **Billing class.** Its billing class must be one the term accepts (Self-Pay Patient Invoice, Insured Patient Responsibility Invoice, Out-of-Network Balance Invoice or Medicare Beneficiary Liability Invoice).
3. **Balance.** Its balance due must be above 0.00.
4. **Invoices in collections.** An invoice in collections must first be recalled under the invoice rules of Patient Invoices & Statements before it can be enrolled; a patient's request alone does not recall it.

## Conditions on the plan

5. **Plan status — no longer in force.** The former clause that invoices can be enrolled only while the plan is pending acceptance or active is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis governing enrollment on a plan.
6. **Adding after acceptance.** After acceptance an invoice may be added only where the term allows invoices to be added after acceptance, only while the plan is active, without the plan carrying more than the term's maximum number of invoices, and without the new plan balance exceeding the term's largest carried balance.
7. **Installment on an addition — no longer in force.** The former clause that the installment is then recomputed over the remaining installments where the term re-amortizes on add, or that the number of installments grows by no more than the term's add-on extension months where it does not, is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for setting the installment when an invoice is added.
8. **Balance that does not fit.** A balance that does not fit is not added; the invoice stays in the statement cycle.

## Invoice status check

| Invoice status in the records | May be enrolled |
|---|---|
| Open | Yes, if the other conditions hold |
| On hold | No |
| In collections | No — not until recalled under the invoice rules |
| Already on a plan | No |
| Paid | No |
| Closed | No |

## Hypothetical additions to an active 12-month plan (largest carried balance 3,000.00, capacity 8 invoices)

- Plan balance 2,600.00, 4 invoices so far; an open Self-Pay Patient Invoice with 350.00 due. New plan balance 2,950.00, 5 invoices: it fits and may be added.
- Same plan; an open invoice with 450.00 due. New plan balance 3,050.00 exceeds 3,000.00: it is not added and stays in the statement cycle.
- Same plan; the invoice is in collections and the patient asks for it to be put on the plan. The request does not recall it, so it cannot be enrolled while it remains in collections.

superseded_clauses: the installment is then recomputed over the remaining installments when re_amortize_on_add is true, or the number of installments grows, by no more than max_term_extension_months_on_add months, when it is false.
Invoices can be enrolled only while the plan status is pending_acceptance or active.
